Operational definition: Repeated units observed at relatively few ordered time points; adding units does not create additional temporal transitions.
Evidence that past x improves the explanation or forward prediction of y after conditioning on past y and declared controls.
A causal interpretation supported by an identification design and assumptions beyond predictive lead-lag evidence.
The prespecified maximum set of delays examined for each direction and predictor-outcome pair.
A transformed series that preserves selected marginal or serial properties while breaking the original temporal alignment.
A randomized or circularly shifted copy used as a negative-control benchmark for machine-learning importance or predictive gain.
Bayes factor comparing the unrestricted model with the restricted model; values above one favor the unrestricted information set.

Corroboration across empirically distinct evidence families: one linear-model family (frequentist and/or Bayesian) and one nonlinear/predictive Random Forest family, plus replication and sensitivity gates.
